question: What caused the production perf-canary paging storm on 2026-02-12 right after canary coverage was expanded (and paging rules were enabled), and what immediate mitigations/config changes were applied to stop the repeated pages?

facts.F1: The paging storm began when paging was enabled immediately after canary coverage was expanded.
facts.F2: The storm exposed a config and telemetry mismatch in the canary baseline lookup: the baseline lookup key included extra or transient labels (such as prompt_bucket and newly emitted runtime or kernel related labels).
facts.F3: Because the baseline lookup key included extra or transient labels, baseline fetches frequently missed and fell back to conservative default thresholds.
facts.F4: High-cardinality labels fragmented metrics into many sparse time series, which broke alert or evaluator minimum sample assumptions and also broke incident-bot or alert deduplication, leading to repeated re-pages.
facts.F5: Immediate mitigation was to silence or disable the paging rules to stop the pages.
facts.F6: Immediate mitigation was to roll back canary coverage to the prior smaller model set.
facts.F7: Immediate mitigation was to pin to fixed baseline artifacts (stop rolling baselines).
facts.F8: A config change was applied to normalize baseline_key_labels to stable labels such as model, model_version, region, sku, and tier.
facts.F9: A config change was applied to drop or stop emitting high-cardinality labels including kernel labels, prompt_bucket, and run, template, or route related labels.
facts.F10: Paging min-sample and dampening were temporarily increased so alerts stopped re-firing.
